digest.headline: The Nasdaq entered a correction as technology stocks slumped and global markets recorded widespread equity declines.

lede.b: The Nasdaq index fell by 3.4% over the week. An index is a group of stocks tracked together to measure market performance. The Nasdaq entered a correction, which means it dropped more than 10% from its recent peak. Artificial intelligence chip stocks dragged down the tech sector. Investor sentiment plunged into extreme fear as futures dropped.
lede.i: The Nasdaq entered a correction after dropping 3.4% over the week amid a slump in artificial intelligence chip stocks. Investor sentiment plunged as the fear gauge hit extreme fear levels. Microsoft-Oracle news added downward pressure to index futures during the tech-led market downturn.
lede.a: The Nasdaq slid into a correction following a 3.4% weekly decline driven by a broad sell-off in artificial intelligence chip names. Investor sentiment reached extreme fear readings while Microsoft-Oracle developments weighed on index futures. Mega-cap tech dominance faced headwinds, prompting record buybacks and strategy rotations.

thread.b: Technology sector sell-offs and artificial intelligence stock drops impacted equity indexes across multiple regions. Major markets experienced increased volatility and downward price revisions over the period.
thread.i: Technology sector liquidations and artificial intelligence share sell-offs drove equity index declines across multiple global markets. Major exchanges absorbed heightened volatility as regional technology stocks faced downward momentum.
thread.a: Cross-border technology sell-offs and artificial intelligence equity corrections drove synchronized downside pressure across major international indices. Regional markets absorbed parallel contractions while dealing with localized currency and sector headwinds.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: Nasdaq enters correction as tech stocks slump

stories.b: The Nasdaq index tracks many technology companies. This index dropped by 3.4% over the week. AI chip stocks experienced a sharp slump. The market fear gauge hit extreme fear.
stories.i: The Nasdaq slid into a correction as AI chip stocks slumped. The index dropped 3.4% over the week. Investor sentiment plunged as the fear gauge hit extreme fear. Microsoft-Oracle news added pressure to futures.
stories.a: The Nasdaq entered correction territory after shedding 3.4% on the week, weighed down by sliding AI chip stocks and Microsoft-Oracle developments. Market sentiment deteriorated to extreme fear on the volatility gauge. Futures tracking the index fell further.

stories.b: Berkshire Hathaway announced a record stock buyback worth $9.6bn. A buyback is when a company purchases its own shares from the market. This move highlights defensive strategies during market stress. Buffett's playbook gained focus as indexes dropped.
stories.i: Berkshire posted a record $9.6bn buyback during the tech-led market downturn. Warren Buffett's crisis playbook drew renewed focus as indexes fell. Investors rotated strategies as mega-cap tech dominance faced headwinds.
stories.a: Berkshire Hathaway executed a record $9.6bn share buyback amidst the broader market sell-off. Buffett's crisis playbook came back into focus as the S&P 500 faced calls to look beyond mega-cap tech. Capital Economics warned that the AI investment boom is fading.

stories.b: Bitcoin achieved a correlation of 0.80 with the S&P 500 index. This index measures the value of 500 large US corporations. The high number means Bitcoin moves in the same direction as major tech shares. Analysts questioned if cryptocurrency trades like a technology stock.
stories.i: Bitcoin reached a 0.80 correlation with the S&P 500 index. The high coefficient raised questions about whether digital assets trade like growth equities. Strong jobs reports simultaneously defied previous rate hikes while breaking primary cycle lows.
stories.a: Bitcoin's correlation coefficient with the S&P 500 touched 0.80, renewing debates on its asset classification relative to tech equities. Concurrently, a robust jobs report defied past rate hikes while the Nasdaq broke primary cycle lows.

politics.b: The US economy expanded at a 3.4% rate in the third quarter. This growth rate beat previous forecasts. A strong jobs report was also published.
politics.i: Third-quarter economic growth beat forecasts to print at a 3.4% annualized rate. A strong jobs report defied prior rate hikes. Markets digested these macroeconomic prints alongside tech sector declines.
politics.a: US gross domestic product expanded at a 3.4% rate in the third quarter, surpassing consensus forecasts. The resilient macroeconomic data accompanied a strong jobs report that complicated the interest rate outlook.

timeline: Berkshire Hathaway announced a record $9.6bn buyback.
Capital Economics warned the AI investment boom is fading.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: Bank of England rate forecasts and FTSE 100 dividends

stories.b: Three banks expect the Bank of England, which sets official borrowing costs, to raise rates in February. Experts also forecast that inflation, the rate at which prices rise, could reach 5%.
stories.i: Three lenders target February for the next rate increase from the central bank. Meanwhile, forecasts indicate that inflation could accelerate to 5%.
stories.a: Three institutions model February as the timing for the next rate hike alongside projections that inflation prints could touch 5%.

stories.b: Companies in the FTSE 100 index, which tracks the largest shares on the London market, plan to pay out more than £80bn in dividends. Dividends are cash payments given to company owners from profits.
stories.i: The FTSE 100 index remains on course to distribute over £80bn in shareholder payouts. These distributions occur while firms operate amid global market uncertainty.
stories.a: The FTSE 100 index aggregates over £80bn in anticipated dividend distributions. Corporations maintain these capital return trajectories despite broader macroeconomic volatility.

politics.b: The UK budget introduced updates affecting travel and tourism alongside calculations for household insurance costs.
politics.i: The recent budget outlined specific measures for the travel and tourism sectors as well as regional insurance impacts.
politics.a: Fiscal policy announcements detailed structural adjustments for travel and tourism alongside localized insurance cost provisions.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: German equities finish flat as technology shares decline

stories.t: DAX 40 Index Closes Flat After Hitting Record High
stories.b: The DAX 40 is a stock index, which is a group of major shares tracked together to show how the market is doing. The DAX finished flat at 25,820.36 points. It hit a record high before dropping 1.92% on Friday.
stories.i: The DAX 40 settled flat at 25,820.36 points following a volatile session. The index touched a record high earlier in the week before experiencing a 1.92% reversal on Friday.
stories.a: The DAX 40 printed a flat weekly close at 25,820.36 points after exhausting its upside momentum. A sharp 1.92% Friday reversal erased intra-week gains that had pushed the benchmark to a record high.

stories.t: German Automotive and Tech Stocks Fall on Chip Concerns
stories.b: Volkswagen shares dropped 2.5% because of problems in the computer chip market. BASF won praise for its automotive plastics. Deutsche Bank faced pressure as it rolled out artificial intelligence tools.
stories.i: Volkswagen shares fell 2.5% amid a broader chip sector rout. BASF received recognition for its automotive plastics despite a technology-led selloff. Deutsche Bank advanced its artificial intelligence rollout against a demanding market backdrop.
stories.a: Volkswagen shares retreated 2.5% under the weight of a semiconductor rout, prompting diverging recovery analyses from Bernstein and HSBC. BASF secured accolades for automotive plastics while broader tech-led liquidation pressured equities. Deutsche Bank pressed forward with its artificial intelligence rollout amidst an unforgiving tape.

politics.b: Germany announced new language requirements for foreign skilled workers seeking jobs in the country.
politics.i: Germany introduced mandatory language requirements for foreign skilled workers applying for employment.
politics.a: Germany instituted formal language proficiency mandates for foreign skilled workers targeting domestic employment opportunities.

timeline: 8 Nov
Germany sets new language rules for foreign skilled workers.

Japan.label: Japan

stories.b: An index is a basket of shares grouped together to track the health of a stock market. The Nikkei 225 index tracks major companies in Japan. This index fell 9.25% in a weekly review. The index closed at 57,434.77. This drop officially pushes the market into a bear market, which is a term used when prices fall significantly from recent highs.
stories.i: The Nikkei 225 index dropped 9.25% in a weekly review. The market move brought the index down to 57,434.77. This decline officially pushed Japanese equities into a bear market. The heavy losses followed a deeper sell-off in artificial intelligence shares.
stories.a: The Nikkei 225 index retreated 9.25% to 57,434.77 over the week. This contraction confirmed a technical bear market designation for Japanese equities. Broader technology sector liquidations, particularly in artificial intelligence equities, drove the downward momentum.

politics.b: No political updates were reported in Japan today.

China.label: China
China.sub: New share listings, payment processing issues, and currency policy

stories.t: Juruisi Prepares For STAR Market Debut
stories.b: Juruisi is a large company that builds direct-drive CNC machine tools. CNC machine tools are automated manufacturing machines controlled by computers. Juruisi will sell its shares to the public on the STAR Market on Nov. 10. Each share will cost 45.37 yuan. The yuan is the official currency of China.
stories.i: Juruisi, a direct-drive machine tool leader, scheduled its listing on the STAR Market for Nov. 10. The company priced its shares at 45.37 yuan each. This initial public offering brings another industrial manufacturer to the domestic exchange.
stories.a: Juruisi set its STAR Market listing date for Nov. 10 with an equity price of 45.37 yuan per share. The direct-drive CNC equipment manufacturer adds liquidity and sector depth to the exchange's roster. Pricing reflects current domestic valuation multiples for specialized industrial hardware producers.

stories.t: Chinese Payment Firm Faces Settlement Freeze
stories.b: A Chinese payment firm is currently dealing with a serious settlement crisis. This crisis leaves many ordinary merchants unable to access or recover their funds. Merchants are people who sell goods and rely on daily cash flow to run their businesses. The blocked payments prevent businesses from operating normally.
stories.i: A settlement crisis at a Chinese payment firm left numerous merchants unable to access funds. Transaction processing bottlenecks trapped merchant revenues within the company's accounts. Affected businesses now face liquidity shortages due to the withheld settlements.
stories.a: A Chinese payment processor encountered a severe settlement breakdown, stranding merchant funds and halting cash withdrawals. Clearing friction and reserve misallocation typically drive such payment gateway freezes. The resulting working capital constraints threaten downstream vendor solvency across the merchant network.

politics.b: European officials exerted pressure regarding the value of the Chinese yuan. Critics want the currency to appreciate or grow in value at a faster rate. Editorial commentary stated that external pressure will not accelerate the appreciation.
politics.i: European pressure mounted on Chinese authorities regarding the appreciation pace of the yuan. Commentators noted that external diplomatic demands will not alter the speed of currency adjustment. Exchange rate policy remains managed according to domestic priorities.
politics.a: European lobbying intensified over the valuation trajectory of the yuan. Commentary pushed back against external pressure to accelerate nominal appreciation. Authorities maintain domestic discretion over the currency basket mechanism regardless of foreign trade friction.

India.label: India
India.sub: Muhurat trading ends flat and Sensex nears 81,000

stories.t: Muhurat Trading Closes Near Flat Following Rally
stories.b: The Nifty 50 stock index dropped 0.2% on November 8. This minor fall stopped an eight-year winning streak for the special Muhurat trading session. The Sensex index finished at 80,999 and the Nifty ended at 24,986. Overall trading ended nearly flat after a seven-day market rally.
stories.i: The Nifty 50 index declined 0.18% on November 8, terminating an eight-year winning streak during the Muhurat session. The Sensex finished at 80,999 while the Nifty settled at 24,986. Trading closed nearly flat following a seven-day market rally.
stories.a: The Nifty 50 contracted 0.18% on November 8, breaking an eight-year consecutive winning streak for the Muhurat session. The Sensex closed at 80,999 alongside a Nifty print of 24,986. The session concluded nearly flat, capping a prior seven-day advance.

stories.t: Foreign Investment Reaches Rs 46,000 Crore in November
stories.b: Foreign institutional investors bought Rs 46,000 crore worth of shares in November. This pushed the Sensex close to the 81,000 mark. Meanwhile, company promoters sold $43bn over the past year.
stories.i: Foreign institutional investors injected Rs 46,000 crore in November, pushing the Sensex toward 81,000. Company promoters liquidated $43bn over the preceding 12 months.
stories.a: Foreign institutional investor inflows reached Rs 46,000 crore in November, driving the Sensex near the 81,000 threshold. Promoter divestments totalled $43bn over the trailing year.

Brazil.label: Brazil

stories.t: Petrobras adopts Cardano and advances field projects
stories.src: Pluang · Ships Monthly · Ocean Energy Resources
stories.b: Petrobras is a big energy company. It started using a digital system called Cardano to track sustainable aviation fuel. It also received approval for a floating production storage and offloading concept at the Tupi Field. Rina won a subsea decommissioning contract from the company too.
stories.i: Petrobras began using the Cardano blockchain to track sustainable aviation fuel. The energy firm advanced its Tupi Field redevelopment after securing LR approval for a floating production storage and offloading concept. Rina secured a subsea decommissioning contract connected to the company.
stories.a: Petrobras integrated the Cardano blockchain to track sustainable aviation fuel shipments. The Tupi Field redevelopment progressed via LR approval for a floating production storage and offloading vessel design. Rina secured the subsea decommissioning contract for related assets.

stories.t: Investors adjust stakes as Petrobras navigates timelines
stories.b: Point Nemo Capital LLC reduced its stake in Petrobras. The energy company raised its credit standing recently. Meanwhile, the start date for Sirius Gas slipped, and diesel cargoes plugged refinery gaps.
stories.i: Point Nemo Capital LLC cut its stake in Petrobras. Petrobras lifted its credit standing while the Sirius Gas start date slipped. Diesel cargoes plugged ongoing refinery gaps for the firm.
stories.a: Point Nemo Capital LLC reduced its equity exposure to Petrobras. Petrobras upgraded its credit standing despite delays to the Sirius Gas startup and refined product deficits filled by diesel cargoes.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia

stories.b: The Houthis launched missiles at an Aramco building in Riyadh. The Energy Ministry reported minor damage to the structure located in the capital's financial district. The attack also targeted oil storage facilities and the Riyadh airport. Saudi supply risk grew following the assault.
stories.i: The Houthis targeted an Aramco building in Riyadh's financial district with missiles, causing minor damage according to the Energy Ministry. Additional strikes targeted Riyadh airport and local oil storage facilities. These developments escalated supply risk for the region.
stories.a: Missiles struck an Aramco facility within Riyadh's financial district, yielding minor structural damage per the Energy Ministry. Concurrently, the operational perimeter experienced attempted strikes targeting the Riyadh airport and associated oil storage. These vectors heightened regional supply risk metrics.

politics.b: The Energy Ministry released details regarding the attempted attack on the building. The Houthis claimed responsibility for the strikes on Riyadh facilities.
politics.i: The Energy Ministry acknowledged the incident with a statement confirming minor damage at the site. The Houthis asserted responsibility for the broader wave of attacks.
politics.a: Official disclosures from the Energy Ministry quantified the physical impact as minor damage. Houthi channels claimed simultaneous responsibility for strikes across the capital's infrastructure.

timeline: Houthis launch missile strikes targeting an Aramco tower in Riyadh.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Foreign exchange market tightness and currency pressures

stories.t: Foreign Exchange Market Shrinks Dollar Liquidity
stories.b: The naira is the official money used in Nigeria. Forex is short for foreign exchange, which is where different national currencies are traded against each other. The supply of US dollars available in this market has tightened recently. This drop in available dollars caused the naira to weaken further.
stories.i: The naira weakened in the foreign exchange market as liquidity tightened. Dollar supply constraints continue to weigh on the domestic currency. Lower availability of foreign exchange drives further depreciation in official trading.
stories.a: Interbank liquidity contractions manifested directly in currency depreciation as dollar scarcity intensified. The structural deficit in foreign exchange supply constrains domestic monetary stability. Marginal clearing rates deteriorated further during the session.

stories.t: Taraba State Enforces Executive Order Against Currency Abuse
stories.src: The Guardian Nigeria News · Daily Post Nigeria
stories.b: Governor Kefas signed an executive order in Taraba State. The new rule stops people from spraying money at public events. Spraying money usually means dancing and throwing cash notes on people. The order aims to stop the misuse of naira notes.
stories.i: Governor Kefas signed an executive order targeting currency abuse in Taraba State. The directive specifically bans the practice of spraying naira notes at public gatherings. Law enforcement mechanisms are now tasked with curbing this physical handling of physical cash.
stories.a: Executive intervention in Taraba State criminalises traditional cash distribution methods at public functions. Governor Kefas utilised administrative powers to enforce statutory currency protection rules. Compliance monitoring will be handled through newly established executive guidelines.

politics.b: Political critics are arguing about who caused the currency to lose value. Campaign groups for opposition figures blame President Tinubu for the falling exchange rate. Other politicians are making promises about what their candidates will do if they win future elections.
politics.i: Opposition campaigns increased pressure on President Tinubu regarding the depreciation of the naira. Critics rejected government claims of an economic recovery. Meanwhile, political parties began establishing campaign infrastructure for the 2027 elections.
politics.a: Political discourse focused heavily on macroeconomic fallout from past currency reforms. Opposition factions disputed administration claims of stabilization, attributing ongoing FX volatility directly to executive policy. Regional actors simultaneously mobilised grassroots support structures ahead of the 2027 electoral cycle.

timeline: Governor Kefas signed an executive order banning naira spraying in Taraba.
The foreign exchange market recorded tighter dollar supply and naira weakness.

stories.i: National Australia Bank selected Ian Saines as chair-elect. The appointment arrives as the banking cycle encounters increased pressure. Ian Saines assumes the role of chair-elect at National Australia Bank.
stories.a: National Australia Bank positioned Ian Saines as chair-elect against a backdrop of tightening operating margins. The transition signals evolving governance demands within the banking sector. Ian Saines formally steps into the chair-elect post at National Australia Bank.
